rationale: The workflow is a single job triggered only by workflow_dispatch, so matrix-based patterns (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST) and push/PR run-cancellation (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE) do not apply. The only pattern with direct measured evidence is P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508), but its artifact applies a 5-minute job timeout to a ~34-second Node.js job, whereas this workflow runs apt installs, multiple git clones, and source builds of SDL3/SDL_image/SDL_ttf/SDL_mixer plus an AppImage. The repository ci_history is explicitly "not_a_measured_baseline", so there is no representative successful-duration history from which to set a safe timeout bound; the pattern's contraindication ("Valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit") and safety tests ("Cold dependency installation", "Slow valid run") cannot be satisfied a priori, and applying a 5-minute bound risks failing valid runs and reducing coverage. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is not reliably applicable: there is no lockfile to key a cache (precondition unmet) and the evidence is pip-based, not apt/git. No supported optimization preserves coverage safely here.
